anchors.paper_title: A foundation model with multi-variate parallel attention to generate neuronal activity
anchors.reason: The abstract explicitly states, 'To support this and future efforts by the community, we release the SWEC iEEG dataset,' confirming the paper introduces this specific dataset.

metadata.methods_description: Intracranial strip, grid, and depth electrodes were recorded with 16-bit analog-to-digital conversion at 512 Hz or 1024 Hz sampling rate. Data were digitally band-pass filtered (0.5–150 Hz, 4th-order Butterworth, zero-phase) and median-referenced across channels. Artifact-contaminated channels were removed at source. Seizure onsets and offsets were annotated by a board-certified epileptologist.

citation_details.title: DIVER-1: Scaling Intracranial EEG Foundation Models for Transferable Representations
citation_details.author: Danny Dongyeop Han, Yonghyeon Gwon, Ahhyun Lucy Lee, Taeyang Lee, Seongjin Lee, Jubin Choi, Sebin Lee, J. Bang, Seungju Lee, David Keetae Park, Shinjae Yoo, Chun Kee Chung, Jiook Cha
citation_details.abstract: Intracranial EEG (iEEG) provides direct, millisecond-scale recordings of human neural activity, but reusable representation learning is difficult because electrode layouts, anatomical coverage, referencing schemes, and recording conditions vary across patients and centers. We introduce DIVER-1, a self-supervised iEEG foundation model for variable-input recordings that combines any-variate electrode-time attention, spatio-temporal resampling, input-conditioned positional embeddings, and multi-domain masked reconstruction without assuming a fixed electrode montage. We pretrain two variants, DIVER-1-0.1s and DIVER-1-1s, on 5,310 hours of ECoG and SEEG spanning 352k channel-hours, roughly 54x the BrainTreeBank-based pretraining volume. We evaluate DIVER-1 on two held-out benchmarks: Neuroprobe for naturalistic cognitive decoding and MAYO for seizure detection. citation_details.title: SWEC iEEG Dataset
citation_details.author: Francesco Carzaniga, Michael Hersche, Abu Sebastian, Kaspar Schindler, Abbas Rahimi
citation_details.abstract: A fully anonymized long-term intracranial EEG dataset from 40 patients with pharmacoresistant epilepsy recorded at the Sleep-Wake-Epilepsy-Center, University of Bern. The dataset comprises 5376 hours of continuous iEEG with 381 annotated electrographic seizures, sampled at 512 or 1024 Hz and preprocessed with band-pass filtering and median referencing. This resource supports development and validation of seizure detection and neuronal activity modeling algorithms.
